plan.title: Alan Turing: The Man Who Taught Machines to Think
plan.description: A short profile of Alan Turing, the British mathematician who imagined the modern computer, helped break Nazi codes, and asked whether machines can think. Learn why his ideas still shape the device in your pocket.

beats.narration: One man helped end a war, invented the idea behind every computer, and was thanked with cruelty. His name was Alan Turing, and his story begins with a question.
beats.chapter: A mind ahead of its time

beats.narration: Turing was a British mathematician born in 1912. Even as a boy, he loved numbers and puzzles, and he saw patterns where other people saw nothing at all.
Decades ago he imagined a simple machine. It would follow simple rules, then write a new symbol, again and again. That tiny idea could, in theory, compute anything.

props.title: The idea of a universal machine

beats.narration: That thought of a machine that could run any program is the seed of the modern computer. Your phone, your laptop and your games all grow from it.

props.alt: hands typing on a laptop keyboard

beats.narration: Then came World War Two. Germany sent secret messages using a machine called Enigma. The codes changed every day, and without a way to read them, ships were at risk.
Turing joined the codebreakers at Bletchley Park in England. He helped design machines that searched for the settings of Enigma much faster than any person could.
Historians widely agree that this work saved many lives and shortened the war. For years it stayed secret, so almost nobody knew what he had done.

props.text: His work shortened the war, and stayed secret for years.

beats.narration: After the war, Turing kept asking big questions. In 1950 he wondered whether a machine could think, and proposed a test where you chat and try to guess who is human.

turns.speaker: Judge
turns.text: Are you a person or a machine?

turns.speaker: Unknown
turns.text: Why don't you guess from my answers?

beats.narration: Today we call it the Turing Test, and it echoes whenever we talk to a chatbot. His question is more alive now than it was then.

props.clip_query: person typing on computer at night
props.alt: working at a computer screen in the dark

beats.narration: Turing was treated cruelly by the law of his time for who he was, and he died young in 1954. Britain later apologized. His legacy is a world built on his thinking.

props.alt: Close view of a circuit board

beats.narration: So the next time you open a screen, remember a quiet mathematician who asked whether machines could think, and gave us the way to find out.

props.text: Every computer begins with one man's question.
